newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota Twins unveil stadium design plans.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota Twins unveil stadium design plans.

text.p: The Minnesota Twins baseball team on Friday unveiled design plans in Minneapolis for a $310 million to $350 million covertible-roof stadium.
The release of a model of the 42,000-seat ballpark came at the end of a week that saw dissatisfaction amoung some state lawmakers over a financing plan for the project.
Earlier this month, Gov. Arne Carlson threw his support behind a 10 cent hike in the state cigarette tax to fund the state's approximately $200 million portion of the project.
The Twin's owner has pledged more than $157.5 million in construction and operating costs and offered the state a 49 percent ownership stake in the team.

Brian Dietz, Carlson's press secretary, acknowledged legislative grumbling over the plan, but pointed out that negotiations were ongoing with the team and that a funding bill had yet to be officially introduced.
"There has been lots of discussion and debate," Dietz said. "I don't think there's a doubt it's an uphill battle."
He added that revenue bonds were a possibility for raising the state's share of the project.
Design plans for the stadium call for a natural grass field, 55 suits, 4,300 club seats and a hall of fame museum.
The team said the design would provide more intimate seating configurations than its current Metrodome home.
